title: RemoteRun
description: A run on another fleet member, as a caller sees it (added in 3.2): response of GET /v1/fleet/runs/{run_id}, and the `run` of a remote submit. It is the executing core's run without its repository path, which stays private to the executing host (docs/d2/part-two-design.md, Decision 4). Every timestamp is the executing core's clock; a caller never compares one with its own clock.

cursor.description: Cursor of the newest event in the run's event log on the executing core.

submitter.description: Who submitted the run, as the executing core established it. For a run submitted over the fleet transport it is `member` with the node name the executing core's trust list gives the caller's key.

base_commit.description: The commit of the aliased checkout the run starts from: the named `base_commit` of the submit, else the executing host's HEAD when it accepted the submit.

deadline.description: When the run must be terminal, on the executing core's clock: its clock at acceptance plus the submit's `deadline_ms`. Null without a deadline.

alias.description: A name the operator of a host gives one of its checkouts. The operator asserts that the same alias names the same repository on each host; the core never infers it and checks only a named commit.

submit_request.description: Body of POST /v1/fleet/runs (added in 3.2), on the control socket and over the fleet transport alike. The node of `agent_id` names the member that executes the run: the caller chooses the host, and nothing schedules. The repository is named by `alias`, as the executing host defines it; no path crosses the network. Optional fields are omitted, never null. No field sets the run's `submitter`.

deadline_ms.description: How long the run may take, in milliseconds, counted on the executing core's clock from when it accepts the submit. A duration, never an absolute time: no timestamp from the caller's clock is sent (spec c42). At most 30 days.

base_commit.description: The full commit id the run must start from. The executing core refuses the submit with `invalid` when its aliased checkout lacks that commit, and fetches nothing. When omitted, the run starts from the executing host's HEAD at acceptance, which the response returns.

submit_response.description: 201 response of POST /v1/fleet/runs. For a new run it is in state `queued`. When `replayed` is true the idempotency key matched an earlier submit of the same member: nothing was created and `run` is that first run as it is now.

replayed.description: True when the request repeated an earlier submit with the same idempotency key. Omitted otherwise.

warnings.description: Things the caller should know about a run that was admitted all the same. Omitted when there are none.

alias_list.description: Response of GET /v1/fleet/aliases (added in 3.2): the aliases a member defines, each with the agent and harness pairs its allow-list permits on the aliased checkout. No path is reported.

node.description: The member whose aliases these are.

alias_file.description: The core's local alias file, `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/culture-agents/fleet/aliases.json` (added in 3.2). Not an API payload: no route reads or writes it, and it is never tracked. Each alias resolves to an absolute path on this host; a submit through it is allowed only when the allow-list permits the agent and harness on that path.
